conditions: Ideal linear spring; x is signed extension relative to its unstretched length; F is the spring force along the same axis. No assertion about the net force from other loads.
spoken_aliases: f equals negative k times x
spring force equals negative spring constant times signed extension

evidence: The linear spring model defines positive stiffness k and restoring force opposite the extension x. Thus F=-kx; the sign restores equilibrium and k has force-per-length units. This is a constitutive law valid within its linear elastic regime.
Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-1-simple-harmonic-motion. Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
